questions.question:
Identify the degree of comparison of the underlined adjective in the following judicial sentence:
"The public prosecutor presented a very persuasive argument before the Division Bench."

options.text: Comparative Degree
Positive Degree
Superlative Degree
Relative Degree

questions.explanation: Sentence mein adjective 'persuasive' apne unmodified base form mein hai. Yahan na toh do entities ke beech '-er / more' se comparison ho raha hai (Comparative) aur na hi group apex isolate kiya gaya hai (Superlative). Adverb 'very' intensifier hai jo Positive Degree adjective ko qualify karta hai. Isliye ye strictly Positive Degree hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Positive Degree represents the base, uncompared quality of an entity.
questions.hint: Check karein ki kya adjective mein '-er', 'more', '-est' ya 'most' laga hai, ya wo apni simple base form mein hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the correctly spelled comparative form of the adjective 'hot' in the sentence:
"Today the courtroom was ___ than yesterday afternoon."

options.text: hoter
hotter
more hot
hottest

questions.explanation: Word 'hot' single-syllable adjective hai jo single consonant 't' par end hota hai aur usse theek pehle single short vowel 'o' hai (CVC pattern). Rule ke mutabiq, '-er' jodne se pehle final consonant double ho jata hai: h-o-t + t + e-r = 'hotter'. Option (A) spelling mistake hai, Option (C) unnecessary periphrasis hai, aur Option (D) superlative form hai jabki sentence mein do din ('today' vs 'yesterday') compare ho rahe hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: CVC Consonant Doubling (Short Vowel + Single Final Consonant).
questions.hint: Jab single vowel ke baad single consonant aaye, toh '-er' lagane par consonant double hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Select the correct comparative form of the adjective 'heavy' in the sentence:
"The legal case file from the subordinate court was ___ than anticipated."

options.text: heavyer
heavier
more heavy
heaviest

questions.explanation: Adjective 'heavy' consonant 'v' ke baad '-y' par end hota hai. Rule ke mutabiq, consonant + 'y' wale adjectives mein '-y' hatakar '-ier' joda jata hai: h-e-a-v + i-e-r = 'heavier'. Option (A) mein 'y' ko retain kiya gaya hai jo spelling error hai. Option (C) non-standard hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Adjectives ending in consonant + 'y' change 'y' to 'i' before '-er'.
questions.hint: Consonant ke baad aane wala 'y' comparative mein 'i' ban jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the grammatically correct comparative adjective:
"The economic condition of the appellant is ___ today than it was last year."

options.text: badder
more bad
worse
worst

questions.explanation: Adjective 'bad' completely irregular root hai. Iska comparative form 'worse' hota hai aur superlative form 'worst' hota hai. English mein '*badder' ya '*more bad' jaise words exist nahi karte. Sentence mein 'than' hai aur do samay ('today' vs 'last year') compare ho rahe hain, isliye comparative 'worse' aayega. Option (D) 'worst' superlative hai jo do entities ke comparison mein nahi lag sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Irregular Adjectives & Suppletion (bad / worse / worst).
questions.hint: 'Bad' ka comparative form completely different word hota hai jo 'w' se start hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the positive sentence of equality into a comparative sentence without altering its intended meaning:
"Rohan is as diligent as Sohan."

options.text: Sohan is more diligent than Rohan.
Sohan is not more diligent than Rohan.
Rohan is more diligent than Sohan.
Sohan is the most diligent clerk.

questions.explanation: Original sentence equality express kar raha hai ('as diligent as') yaani dono barabar mehnati hain. Agar hum Option (A) ya (C) choose karte hain, toh ek doosre se zyada mehnati ban jayega jisse meaning alter ho jayegi. Sahi comparative transformation negative polarity ke sath aati hai: 'Sohan is not more diligent than Rohan' (Sohan Rohan se zyada mehnati nahi hai = dono barabar hain). Option (D) superlative hai jo do logon ke comparison mein invalid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Equality 'as...as' transforms to negative comparative 'not more...than'.
questions.hint: Dono barabar hain. Iska comparative transformation ye kahega ki 'Sohan Rohan se ZYADA mehnati NAHI hai'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the comparative sentence into a positive sentence preserving its exact propositional meaning:
"An aeroplane flies faster than birds."

options.text: Birds do not fly as fast as an aeroplane.
An aeroplane does not fly as fast as birds.
Birds fly as fast as an aeroplane.
Birds fly faster than an aeroplane.

questions.explanation: Original sentence mein aeroplane birds se zyada fast hai (aeroplane > birds). Positive degree mein convert karne ke liye: (1) Inferior entity 'Birds' ko subject banaya; (2) Sentence ko negative banaya ('do not fly'); (3) Adjective ko base positive form mein 'as fast as' ke beech place kiya. Option (B) aeroplane ko slow bana deta hai (meaning flip). Option (C) dono ko equal kar deta hai. Option (D) comparative form mein hi reh jata hai aur meaning ulta kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: S1 + Comp + than + S2 ➔ S2 + not as/so + Positive + as + S1.
questions.hint: Second entity 'Birds' ko shuru mein layein aur sentence ko negative banayein ('do not fly as fast as...').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the correct comparative transformation of:
"Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world."

options.text: Mount Everest is higher than any peak in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other peak in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other peaks in the world.
Mount Everest is not as high as other peaks in the world.

questions.explanation: Superlative 'the highest peak' group ke supreme apex ko represent karta hai. Comparative degree mein transform karte waqt: (1) Everest ko world ki peaks se alag karne ke liye 'any other' lagana mandatory hai; (2) 'Any other' ke baad strictly SINGULAR noun 'peak' aayega ('than any other peak'). Option (A) mein 'other' omitted hai jisse Everest khud se compare hone lagta hai. Option (C) mein plural 'peaks' hai jo 'any other' ke sath grammatically incorrect hai. Option (D) meaning ko ulta kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05 & RC-06: The + Superlative ➔ Comparative + than ANY OTHER + Singular Noun.
questions.hint: 'Higher than' ke baad 'any other' aur singular noun 'peak' hona zaroori hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the comparative sentence into a positive sentence:
"Lead is heavier than any other metal."

options.text: No other metal is as heavy as lead.
No other metals are as heavy as lead.
Very few metals are as heavy as lead.
All other metals are as heavy as lead.

questions.explanation: Original sentence unique apex comparative hai ('heavier than any other metal'). Iska positive transformation 'NO OTHER + Singular Noun' se start hota hai: 'No other metal is as heavy as lead.' Option (B) mein plural noun 'metals' aur plural verb 'are' laga hai jo 'No other' ke formula ke against hai. Option (C) 'Very few' subset group ('one of the') ke liye use hota hai, unique apex ke liye nahi. Option (D) completely affirmative parity state kar raha hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Comparative + than any other + Singular Noun ➔ NO OTHER + Singular Noun + is + as...as.
questions.hint: Unique number-1 metal ke liye positive sentence 'No other + singular noun' se shuru hoga.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.subtopic: Subset Group: 'One of the' to Positive
questions.question:
Choose the correct positive transformation of:
"Ashoka was one of the greatest kings of India."

options.text: No other king of India was as great as Ashoka.
Very few kings of India were as great as Ashoka.
Very few king of India was as great as Ashoka.
Ashoka was as great as any king of India.

questions.explanation: Original sentence mein 'one of the greatest kings' hai, jiska matlab hai Ashoka akela supreme king nahi tha, balki top elite kings mein se ek tha. 'One of the' wale superlative ka positive transformation hamesha 'VERY FEW + Plural Noun + Plural Verb' se hota hai: 'Very few kings of India were as great as Ashoka.' Option (A) 'No other' unique number-1 king bana deta hai (meaning distortion). Option (C) singular 'king' use karta hai jo 'Very few' ke sath grammatically incorrect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: One of the + Superlative + Plural Noun ➔ VERY FEW + Plural Noun + were + as...as.
questions.hint: Jab original mein 'one of the' ho, toh transformation 'No other' nahi balki 'Very few' se shuru hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Find the grammatically correct sentence among the options:
"Iron is a metal."

options.text: Iron is more useful than any metal found in the mine.
Iron is more useful than any other metal found in the mine.
Iron is most useful than any other metal found in the mine.
Iron is more useful than all metal found in the mine.

questions.explanation: Iron khud ek metal hai. Comparative degree mein jab kisi class ke member ko usi class ke baaki members se compare karte hain, toh subject ko exclude karne ke liye word 'other' lagana mandatory hai: 'than any other metal'. Option (A) mein 'other' missing hai jisse Iron khud se compare hone lagta hai. Option (C) mein comparative structure mein superlative 'most' laga diya gaya hai. Option (D) mein 'all' ke baad singular 'metal' lagaya gaya hai jabki 'all other metals' hona chahiye tha.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The 'Any Other' Self-Exclusion Law.
questions.hint: Check karein ki subject ko group se alag karne ke liye 'other' maujood hai aur noun singular hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence comparing two qualities of the SAME person:
"Rohan possesses both courage and prudence in court litigation."

options.text: Rohan is braver than prudent in court litigation.
Rohan is more brave than prudent in court litigation.
Rohan is the bravest than prudent in court litigation.
Rohan is braver than more prudent in court litigation.

questions.explanation: English grammar ka specific exception rule hai: Jab do alag-alag logon ka comparison na ho raha ho balki EK HI PERSON KI DO ALAG QUALITIES ka comparison ho, toh single-syllable adjective hone ke bawjood '-er' suffix use nahi ho sakta. Uske badle strictly 'MORE + base adjective' use hota hai: 'Rohan is more brave than prudent'. Option (A) '-er' suffix use karta hai jo do alag logon ke comparison ke liye hota hai. Option (C) aur (D) grammatically absurd hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Single Entity Two Qualities ➔ Strictly 'MORE [Adj 1] than [Adj 2]'.
questions.hint: Jab ek hi person ki do qualities compare ho rahi hon, toh '-er' prohibited hota hai aur 'more' mandatory hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct construction:
"In official registry seniority, Mr. Joshi is ___ Mr. Sharma by three years."

options.text: senior than
more senior than
senior to
more senior to

questions.explanation: Adjective 'senior' Latin comparative hai jo '-or' par end hota hai. Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) ke sath conjunction 'than' nahi lagta; strictly preposition 'TO' lagta hai. Sath hi, 'senior' already comparative hai, isliye iske pehle 'more' lagana redundant double comparative error hai. Isliye correct answer 'senior to' hai. Option (A) mein 'than' hai, Option (B) mein double comparative aur 'than' hai, aur Option (D) mein 'more' redundant hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Latin Comparatives & Preposition 'To' (senior to, superior to, preferable to).
questions.hint: Latin adjectives ending in '-or' strictly take 'to' (never 'than', never 'more').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09
